milestones.title: Stage 0 - Reproducible reference
milestones.description: FP32 reference and the pinned OPT ReLU positive control pass original numerical gates. Torch 2.12 preserves the BF16 permutation failure; canonical down remains a costly diagnostic. Practical BF16 grouped execution and its cost evidence remain open.

milestones.title: Stage 1 - Hindsight sparsity envelope
milestones.description: Measure individual-neuron, per-layer, and joint omission quality on whole-document and domain splits. Exit requires useful sparsity on unseen modern-model inputs under predeclared quality criteria.

milestones.title: Stage 2 - Physical packing and cache traces
milestones.description: Completed v0.4 development trace study: 72 conditions and four cache budgets. One grouped condition passes the prospective aggregate-PPL and simulated-traffic screen; strongest warm saving is 15.54%. Held-out quality and physical transfer/runtime gates remain open.

milestones.title: Stage 3 - Causal working-set prediction
milestones.description: One-shot v0.7 failures are preserved. Broader causal prediction may combine current input, execution history and residency; analytical refinement is independently open. A complete causal acquisition policy must qualify before runtime.

milestones.title: Stage 4 - Bounded RAM-to-VRAM execution
milestones.description: v0.9 completes synthetic transfer/staging/grouped-execution characterization: at 157.5 MiB, wall 3.207 ms preaggregated pinned transfer versus 15.924 ms serialized gather/transfer/packing/FFN and 0.566 ms resident FFN. This is not exposed critical-path or whole-model speed. Physical paging remains gated on complete causal selection-and-refinement feasibility and same-budget runtime comparisons.

milestones.title: Stage 5b - Corrective refinement runtime
milestones.description: Runtime half split from analytical issue #12. Gate on complete-policy feasibility and bounded execution; preserve input, acquire and add missing contributions before downstream commitment, with charged detector cost and bounded fallback.

milestones.title: Later - Generalization and representation studies
milestones.description: Small OPT architecture and balanced two-model development controls are complete. The ten authored tasks cover code, extraction, arithmetic, copying and in-prompt topic changes; they do not establish held-out agent quality, a scale law or persistent execution state. Larger-model replication and alternative representations retain their separate evidence prerequisites.

milestones.title: Repairability - Are failed causal selections cheaply repairable?
milestones.description: v0.8 completes privileged fixed-mask repair: five aggregate quality/traffic passes on two reused prefixes, one also passing both individual quality lines. No causal/runtime nominee. Explicit current-input/history/residency acquisition and complete-policy feasibility remain open; an inadequate first pass does not block analytical correction.

issues.title: Deliver the reference apparatus and preserve the BF16 numerical failure
issues.body: Build paired SwiGLU packing and fail-closed numerical gates with immutable raw receipts. Completed: all 84 BF16 local checks pass, but 12/18 full-layout checks fail; sparsity is blocked. Separate FP32 control passes and completes 18 configurations. Validation: 22 tests at delivery and source/receipt hash checks. This closes the apparatus task, not a practical BF16 execution policy. Evidence: docs/protocol.md, docs/initial-results.md, results/initial-20260911, docs/releases/v0.1.0.md.

issues.title: Compare calibration-only co-activation packing with native, random, and popularity layouts
issues.body: Completed the declared WikiText pilot: 20,480 calibration tokens and 4,080 next-token predictions across 16 development articles. All correctness gates pass and 24 configurations complete. The tested co-activation heuristic loses to popularity in all four grouped settings; width-32/75% KL difference is +0.02524 with exploratory paired interval [+0.01648,+0.03468]. All 31 tests pass. Preserve this negative result; do not treat completion as the stage's cache/transfer gate. Evidence: docs/packing-pilot-results.md and docs/releases/v0.2.0.md.

issues.title: Isolate BF16 permutation sensitivity with explicit arithmetic controls
issues.body: Compare five arithmetic policies on the six smoke documents under the original tolerances. Completed: original-order down projection is exactly equal to BF16; reduced-precision reduction disabled and FP32 temporary policies still fail. Repeat with saved token/permutation receipts reproduces all 60 raw rows. Inverse gathers are diagnostic and have no performance claim. A deployable BF16 policy remains a separate open task. Evidence: docs/packing-pilot-results.md and results/packing-pilot-20260911/precision-receipted.

issues.title: Establish a practical BF16 grouped execution policy without relaxing numerical gates
issues.body:
The canonical-order diagnostic is exact but materializes inverse gathers. Define and measure an execution policy that satisfies the original all-weight gates while supporting group-local execution. Charge precision conversion and temporary allocations; preserve original failures and compare all six documents plus a larger sample. Exit: passing function checks and explicit cost evidence, not a relaxed tolerance.

Bound this workstream after the v0.7 design review: retain FP32 mathematical/selection diagnostics and every original BF16 failure. Compare a limited set of grouped policies against a common higher-precision reference with predeclared downstream criteria. Do not launch successive library-version sweeps or replace reference-fidelity limits with task tolerances.

issues.title: Validate PyTorch 2.12 CUDA as a separate environment control
issues.body: Completed the isolated Python 3.14.3 torch/torchvision environment pair: 2.10.0/0.25.0 versus 2.12.0/0.27.0, CUDA 13.0, with every other effective package version aligned. Both full suites pass 59 tests. The 2.10 repeat reproduces all 60 archived arithmetic rows exactly; 2.12 still fails four of five policies under original numerical limits. Canonical down order is exact within each environment. Ordinary dense BF16 outputs differ across all six documents: L2 0.015831-0.024369, KL 0.001018-0.001567, top-1 agreement 95.51-98.78%. Complete inventories, pinned inputs, source snapshots, original failure receipts and manifest-bound logits are preserved. Initial shared torchvision was incompatible and the matching companion resolved it; this is not an unqualified torch-only attribution. This closes the environment-control experiment, not practical BF16 grouping. Evidence: docs/torch212-protocol.md, docs/torch212-results.md, results/torch-control-20260911, docs/releases/v0.5.0.md. Optional shared torchaudio retains a torch-2.10 dependency and is outside the validated text-model path.

issues.title: Add the original plan's ReLU positive control
issues.body: Completed the pinned OPT-1.3B FP32 ReLU control: 80 calibration / 16 development articles, 19,054 calibration tokens and 3,828 scored predictions. All 72 local plus 48 full-layout checks and all 192 exact-zero checks pass under original limits. About 96.04% of neurons are exactly zero; popularity exact-zero selection requires 19.80/40.10/60.40% of FFN bytes at widths 8/32/128. Fixed 75% width-128 popularity retention has relative PPL 1.014112 versus native 1.074781. Preserve all 545 raw rows, 24 aggregates, biased-projection accounting, immutable source and inputs, and the first incomplete-checkpoint failure. No transfer, bounded residency, runtime or SwiGLU generalization claim. Validation: 89 tests and independent ledger/aggregate validation. Evidence: docs/relu-control-protocol.md, docs/relu-control-results.md, results/relu-control-20260911, docs/releases/v0.6.0.md.

issues.title: Measure per-layer omission sensitivity and joint-layer interaction
issues.body: Completed the predeclared 66-condition per-layer and fixed-block study on all 28 FFNs, reusing frozen popularity/co-activation layouts and the 16 development articles. All 88 correctness checks pass; 1,056 document measurements are preserved. Top-four layers account for 20.82% / 19.57% of single-layer KL sums, and all 32 joint-layer document controls reproduce the parent quality metrics exactly. Co-activation improves single-layer KL in four layers; the complete curves preserve those exceptions and the lower-PPL/higher-KL middle-block result. Validation: 38 tests, reviewed provenance/interruption/plot checks, full raw-aggregate and weight-accounting verification. This closes the bounded experiment, not Stage 1 held-out quality. Evidence: docs/layer-study-protocol.md, docs/layer-study-results.md, results/layer-study-20260911, docs/releases/v0.3.0.md.

issues.title: Establish whole-document multi-domain held-out quality gates
issues.body:
Build separate calibration/development/final-test document sets across code, arithmetic, copying, instructions, multilingual text, and topic switches. Declare task and perplexity tolerances before final scoring. Include per-layer and joint omissions, confidence intervals, and task outcomes; do not replace failed rows or retune against final test. Current Wikipedia pilot is development evidence only.

Development update after v0.10.0 / #20: the separately authored ten-task mix is balanced code, extraction, arithmetic, copying and in-prompt topic changes. Both dense checkpoints score 0/10 under the frozen plain-text whole-output exact rule. All numerical controls pass and the raw outputs/logits are retained, but this endpoint cannot establish preservation of useful agent behavior with such weak dense baselines. No final held-out set was evaluated. Before adopting a task utility gate, preregister a viable dense baseline, instruction format and fresh task set; do not rescore the ten published prompts under a more permissive rule. The broader whole-document and multi-domain held-out gate remains open.


v0.11.0 isolates chat formatting and dense-path fidelity: 7/10 debug and 12/20 fresh successes, all path comparisons pass, but the prospective balanced utility gate fails (14/20 required and topic changes only 1/4). This provides genuine dense successes but not a qualified balanced baseline. Preserve the failure; any interface/model/scoring follow-up needs a new protocol and fresh evaluation.

issues.title: Measure transfer amplification and bounded-cache traces at realistic group sizes
issues.body: Completed all 72 declared layout/width/retention conditions, 1,152 applied-mask traces, 36,864 document replay rows and 2,304 aggregates. Original numerical gates pass and 256 overlapping parent quality rows reproduce exactly. Only popularity/width 8/90% retention passes the prospective development screen: relative PPL 1.008978 and best simulated warm saving 15.54% with the 2 GiB equal-layer static cache. Nine of 16 documents individually exceed 1% PPL increase. LRU has zero hits under the validated distinct-other-layer bound; cold static preload and incoming reserve are charged. Full trace payloads are a hashed release asset. This completes the bounded trace experiment, not held-out quality or actual transfer/runtime gates. The frozen ordering nominates this condition for causal prediction. Evidence: docs/cache-trace-protocol.md, docs/cache-trace-results.md, results/cache-trace-20260911, docs/releases/v0.4.0.md.

issues.title: Compare causally available working-set predictors and their charged cost
issues.body:
Compare static popularity, last-token/window reuse, EMA and learned selectors with explicit feature availability, charged predictor storage and execution cost, independent omission audits, and approximate closed-loop evaluation. Measure quality/bytes/cost curves and topic transitions. Gate: useful proximity to hindsight at an affordable measured cost.

The first frozen-point experiment is complete in #15 / [v0.7.0](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/releases/tag/v0.7.0). All four causal selectors fail quality at Qwen popularity/width 8/90% retention: aggregate relative PPL 1.089204-1.158203 versus <=1.01, and all 16 articles individually fail for each selector. All pass the >=10% simulated warm-traffic screen; recency/EMA/learned also fail the <=10% CUDA-and-wall cost screen at about 72-83%. Static is cheap but loses quality. Incremental hindsight reaches 1.009318 and is ineligible. The complete raw ledger, masks, transition, generation and timing evidence are published.

This issue remains open for the broader useful-predictor gate and curves. No selector is nominated for paging/refinement. The negative result applies to these initial eager implementations and one operating point; it is not a proof that all predictors fail. Faster execution alone does not change the measured mask quality. Any new predictor, retention sweep or scale control needs a separate prospective protocol with fresh immutable receipts. Preserve this failed experiment and the original thresholds; do not retune on final test. Held-out quality #8 and runtime/refinement #11/#12 retain their separate gates.


Prospective dependency revision after the design review: analytical refinement can start from these failed first passes under #12. Explicitly combine current-input evidence, execution history/change signals and resource state in a separate causal acquisition experiment. Runtime nomination concerns the complete policy; v0.7's original one-shot rule is preserved as historical evidence.

issues.title: Implement bounded FFN residency with measured RAM-to-VRAM traffic
issues.body:
Physical paging remains gated on a qualifying complete causal acquisition policy, with or without refinement; its initial pass need not qualify alone. Implement bounded CPU-backed groups, pinned staging and GPU slots only after that gate. Compare against strongest same-budget streaming, static/recency/activation-aware caches and CPU execution, charging scheduling, packing, transfers, synchronization, KV and workspaces. Exit requires measured end-to-end benefit.

The bounded hardware-cost characterization can proceed independently without a model pager. The 10% resident-FFN cost screen remains v0.7's historical rule, not a universal necessary condition for transfer-bound workloads. Exposed transfer stalls must be measured on the actual critical path; isolated timings cannot establish a speedup.

issues.title: Establish analytical selection-and-refinement feasibility
issues.body:
Determine whether an inadequate initial computation can be repaired economically, then whether causally available evidence can request that repair. The complete causal selection-and-refinement policy is the unit of feasibility; the first pass need not qualify by itself. Physical loading/refinement runtime remains separately gated in #11/#16. Preserve the historical v0.7 failures and thresholds.

The privileged diagnostic #17 is complete in v0.8.0: five of 48 fixed-mask repair settings pass aggregate relative PPL <=1.01 and warm simulated saving >=10% on two reused 128-token article prefixes. Recency-hindsight-28 also passes both individual quality lines; the other four pass one of two. None of 20 fresh one-shot conditions passes both aggregate lines. Original masks on corrected trajectories are counterfactual and dense omission scores are privileged. No causal or runtime nominee exists.

The hardware characterization #18/v0.9.0 establishes primitive staging/gathering/transfer/grouped-execution costs, not exposed critical-path savings. The separate balanced two-model development control #20/v0.10.0 records code, extraction, arithmetic, copying and in-prompt topic changes; it is not held-out agent quality or persistent execution-state evidence.

Remaining work is #19: causally regenerate choices and observed state on the corrected trajectory, combine current-input evidence, execution history, residency and charged partial-execution/probe signals, and compare the completed policy with larger initial subsets and explicit fallback. Freeze its protocol, information access, grids and decision rules before scoring. This broad feasibility issue and its milestone remain open.

Evidence: https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/releases/tag/v0.8.0 and https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/releases/tag/v0.9.0. Accepted gate decision: docs/adr/0001-selection-and-refinement-gates.md.

issues.title: Replicate useful results on a larger model and another architecture
issues.body:
After a useful small-model frontier, run a pinned 7B-class dense model and a second family such as Granite or LFM2. Validate real pretrained adapters and preserve architecture-specific normalization/mixing. Compare practical utility with optimized quantized resident models and smaller models at comparable quality/memory. A small-model negative result may justify a limited scale control; it does not justify an unrestricted runtime build.

The bounded Qwen/OPT balanced development control is complete in #20/v0.10.0. OPT hindsight preserves answer/full-text probabilities to numerical tolerance and all ten generated paths; Qwen hindsight raises answer PPL about 2% and matches only one complete generated path. Both dense exact-output baselines score 0/10. These ten plain-text prompts, different tokenizers/training/instruction tuning and unequal model sizes do not isolate an architectural effect, establish useful agent quality, or constitute a 7B scale replication. Preserve the bounded results; the broader generalization issue remains open under its original prerequisites.

issues.title: Evaluate quantization, residual representations, and storage paging as separate branches
issues.body: Keep quantization metadata aligned with neuron permutations and revalidate the function. Study heterogeneous groups, limited lookahead, low-rank-plus-residual decomposition, or training for block structure one change at a time; do not assume residuals are sparse or cheap. For NVMe/SSD work verify actual device reads, RAM cache residency, and swap. MTP integration, Bayesian state, and an always-on service remain deferred until core gates justify them.

issues.title: Deliver the first causal selector experiment at the frozen Qwen operating point
issues.body:
Completed the first causal selector experiment at the unchanged v0.4 Qwen popularity/width-8/90% condition and 2 GiB equal-layer static cache. None of the four causal selectors passes the frozen screen. Static, recency, EMA and learned relative PPL are 1.158203, 1.117159, 1.111589 and 1.089204; every causal selector exceeds 1% on all 16 development articles. All meet the simulated warm traffic screen (15.103-18.663% saving). Static costs 0.450% CUDA / 0.456% wall of paired resident dense FFNs; recency, EMA and learned cost about 72-83%, above the 10% affordability screen. Incremental hindsight reaches relative PPL 1.009318 and 15.539% warm saving, but is noncausal and cannot qualify.

The protocol/apparatus were pushed as [85efbc7](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/commit/85efbc771b75487b7aecfe0c521c1d3e4fd5452e) before fitting/evaluation. All 28 local plus 17 incremental layout gates pass under original 0.01 relative-L2 / 0.001 KL limits. Retain 307 raw rows, 85 document masks/audits, 20 generated-path traces, four dense continuations, 17 dense reference episodes, calibration statistics and fitted weights. All modes complete every article, the fixed topic transition and four closed-loop continuations. Persistent selector tensors reduce simulated FFN-cache capacity; query and necessary update cost are measured separately from the dense diagnostic.

Validation: 111 tests in both baseline torch 2.10 and separate torch 2.12 environments. The independent analyzer checks provenance, complete grids and ordering, numerical gates, actual reference NLL, charged mask replay, timing medians, generation receipts and every aggregate. Restoring all 124 payloads from three hashed release assets reproduces the validated analysis exactly.

This closes a bounded experiment, not the Stage 3 milestone or broader useful-predictor goal #10. Held-out quality #8 stays open. Physical paging #11 and refinement #12 remain gated. No physical transfer, bounded residency, task accuracy or speedup claim; full model and restoration copies remain resident. Predictor initialization traffic/time are excluded from replay, and the cost result covers the measured eager implementations. No final-test score or threshold/retention retuning follows from the failure.

Evidence: [v0.7.0 release](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/releases/tag/v0.7.0), [complete findings](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/blob/v0.7.0/docs/causal-control-results.md), [protocol](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/blob/v0.7.0/docs/causal-control-protocol.md), [archive and restoration](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/tree/v0.7.0/results/causal-control-20260911).

issues.title: Implement bounded refinement runtime after complete-policy feasibility
issues.body:
Preserve the FFN input, acquire missing disjoint group contributions, add them before downstream commitment, and provide bounded dense fallback. Compare silent quality failure against all additional bytes, execution and scheduling latency, including detector cost, versus selecting more initially. Residency misses and unsafe omissions remain distinct.

This is the runtime half split from #12 after the v0.7 design review. It remains gated on feasibility of the complete causal selection-and-refinement policy and bounded physical execution in #11. The first-pass selector does not need to pass alone. Privileged repair traces do not satisfy this gate. The v0.7 negative result and thresholds remain unchanged.

issues.title: Measure privileged and resident-first repair of the frozen v0.7 masks
issues.body:
# v0.8.0 - Failed selections can be repaired in a narrow privileged diagnostic

Five of 48 fixed-mask repair settings pass the predeclared **aggregate relative
PPL <=1.01 and simulated warm transfer saving >=10%** screen. None of 20 fresh
larger one-shot settings passes both. Recency plus 28 hindsight-selected additions
also passes the quality line on both articles; the other four aggregate-passing
settings pass on one article each. **No causal policy or runtime is nominated.**

This is the first test of correction after an inadequate initial selection. It uses
the first two v0.7 development articles, truncated prospectively to 128 input tokens
each: 256 input visits and 254 predicted tokens. It is a small reused development
sample, not held-out confirmation or a replacement for v0.7's 16-article failure.
The original protocols, thresholds and results remain unchanged.

| Initial selector / repair schedule | Additions per layer visit (resident + cold) | Final FFN fraction | Relative PPL | Warm saving | Article passes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| recency-hindsight-28 | 9.213 + 18.787 | 92.500% | 1.005318 | 11.774% | 2/2 |
| recency-resident_first-8 | 22.042 + 8.000 | 92.682% | 1.008490 | 13.572% | 1/2 |
| ema-hindsight-28 | 0.436 + 27.564 | 92.500% | 1.009740 | 13.792% | 1/2 |
| ema-resident_first-28 | 1.157 + 28.000 | 92.603% | 1.009784 | 13.719% | 1/2 |
| learned-resident_first-28 | 10.136 + 27.951 | 93.401% | 1.009158 | 11.177% | 1/2 |

All repairs start with 1,008 of 1,120 width-8 groups in each of 28 Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct
FFNs. The hindsight schedule adds up to its limit from the omitted groups. The
resident-first schedule first includes every omitted resident group, then adds up
to its limit in cold groups. Additions are averaged over all layer visits. Resident
work avoids new transfer in this cache simulation but still adds computation.

The initial masks are frozen from the original causal trajectories. After correction
changes an input, those old masks are counterfactual choices. Repair ranking also
uses current dense activations. These are privileged, heuristic diagnostics; even
the resident-only variants are not causal corrected-policy rollouts or optimal oracles.

## What residency changes

For the learned selector on this sample, the uncorrected relative PPL is 1.114143.
Adding only omitted resident groups reduces it to **1.054495**, with no added cold
traffic relative to the equally charged initial replay. Adding a further average
27.951 cold groups per layer visit reaches **1.009158**, using 93.401% of FFN group
volume and retaining **11.177%** simulated warm saving. The additional cold volume is
**0.107479 GiB per input token**. Its second article still has relative PPL 1.023071.

Recency's resident-first eight-cold-group setting restores an average 22.042 resident
groups plus eight cold groups per layer visit: only **0.030762 GiB** of additional
cold traffic per input token. Aggregate relative PPL is 1.008490, but article values
0.989118 and 1.028240 show the cancellation hidden by the aggregate.

```mermaid
xychart-beta
    title "Learned selector: resident-first repair on two article prefixes"
    x-axis ["Initial", "Resident", "+8 cold", "+28 cold", "+56 cold", "+84 cold", "Full"]
    y-axis "Perplexity increase over dense (%)" 0 --> 12
    line [11.41426, 5.44950, 1.54330, 0.91580, 1.23550, 1.01470, 0.00000]
    line [1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1]
```

The second line is the 1% diagnostic line. More corrective work does not produce a
monotonic perplexity curve: each condition creates its own downstream trajectory,
and contribution-norm ranking does not optimize NLL. The complete report includes
all 68 conditions and both article scores rather than only the passing settings.

## Evidence, accounting and validation

The prospective protocol and apparatus were committed and pushed as
[f2d0cf6](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/commit/f2d0cf6) before measurement. The original FP32 CUDA environment
was used; all **56** controls pass: native-reference reproduction, every local grouped
FFN reconstruction, full layout reconstruction, exact original-selector masks,
zero-repair reproduction and full-repair reconstruction. The run preserves **260
ledger rows, 144 applied-mask/audit traces and 10 reference-logit payloads**.

Repairs preserve the FFN input and add a separate down-projection contribution before
downstream commitment. Dense gate/up tensors, audit computation, the full model and
restoration copies remain in the apparatus. Skipped weights are only analytical.
Original selector storage plus **1,034,880 repair-metadata bytes** reduce the 2 GiB
FFN-cache capacity, with an incoming group reserved. The comparison is the strongest
full-budget dense static layout; its warm traffic is **2.306854 GiB per input token**.
Small negative savings at full restoration reflect charged metadata. Selector startup,
real loading, repair latency, bounded model residency and end-to-end speed are unmeasured.

Independent analysis validates source Git blobs, frozen inputs, reference NLL,
selector reproduction, every repair union and ranking receipt, charged cache replay,
the full grid and all aggregates. Both release ZIPs are checked payload by payload;
a clean restoration must reproduce the analysis. The complete CPU fixture suite has
147 tests in each available PyTorch environment; final clean-tip validation is retained
in the publication receipt. No pretrained scoring is repeated for publication.

## Resulting dependency

The accepted [gate ADR](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/blob/v0.8.0/docs/adr/0001-selection-and-refinement-gates.md)
allows analytical correction from a failed first pass. The **complete causal
selection-and-refinement policy** must qualify before physical paging or refinement
runtime. This delivery closes bounded [#17](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/issues/17), while analytical
feasibility [#12](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/issues/12), causal acquisition [#19](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/issues/19), runtime
[#16](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/issues/16), paging [#11](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/issues/11) and held-out quality remain open.

The next causal test should combine current input, observed execution history and
residency, charging any probes and abstention/fallback. These curves identify an
opportunity worth predicting; they do not establish that an affordable causal signal
exists. Separate hardware-cost and balanced two-model controls proceed under their
own prospective protocols.

[Complete findings and all curves](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/blob/v0.8.0/docs/refinement-feasibility-results.md),
[prospective protocol](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/blob/v0.8.0/docs/refinement-feasibility-protocol.md),
[immutable archive and restoration instructions](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/tree/v0.8.0/results/repair-control-20260911).

issues.title: Characterize grouped execution, staging and transfers without building a pager
issues.body:
# v0.9.0 - Staging and aggregation materially change acquisition costs

This research prerelease completes the bounded hardware-cost experiment in issue #18.
At the full Qwen-shaped layer payload (1,120 width-8 groups, 157.5 MiB), median
synchronized wall times are **3.207 ms** for preaggregated pinned H2D,
**10.544 ms** for pageable staging plus H2D, **13.814 ms** for scattered gathering plus
H2D, **11.405 ms** for individual pinned group copies, **0.566 ms** for resident FFN
execution, and **15.924 ms** for the serialized gather/transfer/packing/FFN path.

These are synthetic primitives on the RTX 5080 Laptop in the original FP32 environment.
They do not measure exposed transfer stalls, overlap, a model pager or inference speed.
All 36 workload/size conditions pass payload or numerical integrity checks before
timing. All 569 raw rows, including warmups, and all 38 timing aggregates are retained.

| Full-layer workload | CUDA interval (ms) | Synchronized wall (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|
| pinned_aggregate | 3.077072 | 3.207250 |
| pageable_staged | 10.409600 | 10.543900 |
| gather_staged | 13.688768 | 13.813800 |
| pinned_individual | 11.196096 | 11.404800 |
| resident_ffn | 0.327568 | 0.566500 |
| gather_transfer_pack_ffn | 15.431056 | 15.923600 |

```mermaid
xychart-beta
    title "Full-layer synthetic acquisition: synchronized wall medians"
    x-axis ["Pinned batch", "Stage + H2D", "Gather + H2D", "Individual", "Resident FFN", "Combined"]
    y-axis "Milliseconds" 0 --> 17
    bar [3.207250, 10.543900, 13.813800, 11.404800, 0.566500, 15.923600]
```

For this payload, staging/gathering and individual dispatch cost substantially more
than the preaggregated transfer. Preaggregation itself is a startup cost excluded
from the pinned-batch workload; its advantage requires those bytes to be ready in
that layout. The combined path includes GPU packing and FFN computation serially.
Workload differences are observations, not a model of overlap or additive timing.

## Ranking is a separate implementation opportunity

For 32 tokens x 28 layers x 1,120 unique scores, keeping 1,008 groups, stable argsort/scatter
costs **62.414 ms CUDA / 62.461 ms wall**. Unsorted topk/scatter costs
**24.918 ms CUDA / 24.957 ms wall**. Masks agree on all 896 unique-score fixtures.
Topk is about 2.50 times faster on this fixture. The all-equal-score masks also agree
in this run; one fixture does not establish general tie equivalence. This result does not authorize a semantics-changing
replacement in frozen selectors. It also cannot repair their measured quality failures.

These timings cover ranking only, not the full learned/current-history predictor,
state update, probes, or correction policy. Dividing by 32 gives a descriptive fixture
cost per token across 28 layers; it is not a whole-model decoding benchmark.

## Protocol, evidence and limits

The protocol and apparatus were committed and pushed as
[b1be0e4](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/commit/b1be0e4) before timing. The measured grid is 1/8/32/128/512/1,120
groups, six workloads, three warmups and ten measured repetitions. Each group holds
all three width-8 projections at hidden 1,536 in FP32: 147,456 bytes. TF32 is disabled,
four CPU threads are used, and the GPU timing window was isolated from other project
GPU experiments and CPU reviews/tests.

The apparatus preallocates a pageable pool, pinned pool, staging, GPU group storage
and canonical gate/up/down matrices. Allocations, seeded initialization, index planning
and initial preaggregation are outside steady-state timing. The event pair is initialized
and reused. Both clocks cover the full submitted interval; CUDA intervals can contain
host submission gaps. Wall times include Python dispatch and synchronization overhead.
The run does not separately measure cold allocation, long-run variance or thermal effects.

Exact copy checks poison destination/staging first. FFN checks compare with a CPU FP32
reference at the original <=0.01 relative-L2 line. The pool SHA-256, permutation and
input are regenerated independently from the frozen seed. Analysis verifies source
Git blobs, the complete ordered ledger, dimensions, accounting, gates, medians and
ranking tie receipts. Tensor payload bytes and allocator peaks through the repetitions
are reported separately; payload counts are not total process memory.

The complete CPU suite passes 158 tests in both available PyTorch environments. All raw
measurements and source snapshots are small enough to remain in Git, with an indexed
archive and an independently reproduced analysis. No model scoring was performed.

The historical v0.7 resident-FFN selector screen remains unchanged. These measurements
show why that screen alone cannot decide memory-constrained runtime economics:
a future complete policy must pay for its decisions, staging, extra execution and
acquisition using actual avoided critical-path time. Conversely, cheap ranking alone
cannot establish efficient loading. Physical paging/refinement runtime remain gated.

This closes bounded [#18](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/issues/18), leaving the Stage 4 runtime milestone,
[#11](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/issues/11), causal acquisition [#19](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/issues/19) and refinement runtime
[#16](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/issues/16) open. No gate threshold is replaced by this characterization.

[Complete 36-condition findings](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/blob/v0.9.0/docs/hardware-cost-results.md),
[prospective protocol](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/blob/v0.9.0/docs/hardware-cost-protocol.md),
[raw archive and reproduction](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/tree/v0.9.0/results/hardware-cost-20260911).

issues.title: Test complete causal acquisition from current input, history and residency
issues.body:
Test whether affordable, causally available evidence can choose corrective computation after an imperfect first pass. This is the next decisive experimental question after #17/v0.8.0. Five privileged repair settings meet aggregate quality/traffic on a tiny reused sample; only one also passes both individual prefixes. Those fixed old masks cannot stand in for a corrected causal rollout.

Before measurement, commit and push a protocol that defines:

- Initial selection and current FFN input features, persistent state updates from actually observed groups, an innovation/change signal, and cache residency/transfer prices.
- Evidence obtained from partial execution before downstream commitment. Every probe and additional acquisition is charged; dense omitted activations and hindsight labels remain isolated evaluation/calibration information and never enter a development query.
- Conservative safe-to-omit decisions with abstention/fallback, compared with current-input-only prediction, static resident-core execution, larger one-shot selection and dense fallback. Recompute initial and repair decisions on each corrected trajectory; do not reuse old development masks.
- Separate calibration and development inputs, reset rules, complete teacher-forced and generated paths, fixed quality/byte criteria, per-document failures, and measured selector/update/refinement overhead. Judge completed output, not first-pass adequacy.
- A prospective interpretation of hardware affordability informed by #18/v0.9.0. Preserve the v0.7 resident-FFN screen as historical; synthetic serialized primitives are not exposed transfer stalls or end-to-end speedup evidence.

Use the balanced development observations in #20/v0.10.0 as limited context, not final-test success. The topic-change fixtures reset KV between tasks and do not validate persistent execution state. Keep held-out #8, broader scale/architecture #13, physical paging #11 and refinement runtime #16 separate. Do not expand into a model sweep, general Bayesian filter, hierarchical representation or always-on service without their recorded prerequisites.

Outcome required: a fully causal quality/acquired-byte/overhead curve with complete raw receipts and explicit failure/nomination decision. A qualifying diagnostic policy can justify the next bounded runtime experiment; achieved memory and latency gains still require physical execution evidence.


Post-v0.10 review sharpens the experiment: allow one corrective acquisition round per FFN before commit or bounded dense completion; separate detection from acquisition. Collect calibration labels on approximate/corrected trajectories. Make matched larger one-shot and resident-first predetermined additions central controls, so improved prediction or greater retention alone cannot establish the value of partial evidence. Charge batch preparation, observation, resident computation, cold acquisition and fallback; report rounds and fallback frequency alongside bytes. No free dynamically preassembled sparse payloads.

Dense interface qualification in #21 is a separate Gate A. Completed causal-policy quality (Gate B) and complete-action economics (Gate C) govern runtime nomination. A failing dense utility baseline blocks utility claims, not the mathematical repair experiment. The accepted decision is docs/adr/0002-qualified-utility-and-causal-evidence.md.


v0.11.0 finds a useful but unqualified dense chat endpoint: 12/20 fresh successes, below the frozen 14/20 and domain minima. Analytical causal repair proceeds independently; this result cannot support a qualified balanced-utility preservation claim.

issues.title: Run one small second-model control on separate balanced development tasks
issues.body:
# v0.10.0 - Both dense baselines score zero on the fixed exact-output tasks

Both dense baselines score **0/10** under the frozen plain-text, whole-output exact
answer rule. OPT static selection scores 1/10; every other masked condition scores 0/10.
This task endpoint cannot demonstrate preservation of useful agent behavior with
these weak dense baselines. The records include formatting failures and substantively
wrong answers, not only a strict parser penalty. No first-line rescoring or prompt
repair follows from this outcome.

This prerelease completes the separately authored ten-task control: **two tasks each
for code, data extraction, arithmetic, exact copying and topic changes**, as requested
for the intended agent. The frozen Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and OPT-1.3B checkpoints are
compared with their own dense outputs using their earlier calibration-only popularity
layouts. No task is replaced, refitted or accepted manually after scoring.

| Model / condition | Exact targets | Answer relative PPL | Answer KL | Full-text relative PPL | Selected FFN volume |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| qwen dense | 0/10 | 1 (reference) | 0 (reference) | 1 (reference) | 100% |
| qwen static | 0/10 | 1.913061 | 0.467378 | 1.434928 | 90.000000% |
| qwen hindsight | 0/10 | 1.019995 | 0.060952 | 1.031498 | 90.000000% |
| opt dense | 0/10 | 1 (reference) | 0 (reference) | 1 (reference) | 100% |
| opt static | 1/10 | 1.041058 | 0.168180 | 1.677362 | 90.039670% |
| opt hindsight | 0/10 | 0.999999 | 0.000000 | 1.000000 | 90.039670% |

Exact targets require the entire decoded text before tokenizer EOS, stripped only of
surrounding whitespace, to equal the frozen answer. Additional output is wrong. All
32 greedy generated IDs, including EOS and subsequent IDs, remain in the ledger.
Answer-only PPL predicts the answer starting at the last prompt token; full-text PPL
also includes the prompt. These denominators answer different questions. Absolute
PPL is not compared across tokenizers, and literal code answers are not execution tests.

Model completion states are **qwen: completed** and
**opt: completed**. The archive contains 138 raw rows, and
72/72 local/full-layout numerical controls pass.
The control reports every per-task output and metric; a model's poor dense baseline
must remain visible when interpreting changes under omission. Ten fixtures provide
only a bounded development observation, not general agent or held-out task accuracy.
Topic-change fixtures switch instructions within a prompt; KV resets between tasks.
This does not test persistent execution state, cross-task residency or long conversations.

```mermaid
xychart-beta
    title "Exact target and format compliance on ten frozen tasks"
    x-axis ["Qwen dense", "Qwen static", "Qwen hindsight", "OPT dense", "OPT static", "OPT hindsight"]
    y-axis "Tasks correct out of 10" 0 --> 10
    bar [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0]
```

Hindsight uses current dense activations and is privileged. These bars do not nominate
a causal policy or establish improved general capability.

## What the omission measurements establish

Qwen static retention raises answer perplexity by 91.306%, while hindsight raises it
by 2.000%. Qwen hindsight agrees with dense top-1 predictions on all 42 teacher-forced
answer tokens, yet only 1/10 complete generated continuations matches dense; mean
agreement across its 32 generated tokens is 37.188%. Teacher-forced answer agreement
therefore does not establish matching closed-loop output on these prompts.

OPT hindsight preserves answer/full-text probabilities to numerical tolerance and
all 10 generated continuations exactly. Its static mask raises answer perplexity by
4.106% and full-text perplexity by 67.736%. The single exact static answer is the
copy-case identifier; one success against a zero-success dense baseline does not
establish improved general capability. The answer-token denominators are 42 for Qwen
and 34 for OPT, each within its own tokenizer; domains still have two tasks each.

The no-chat-template plain-text format and exact-output requirement are material
limitations of this frozen control. For example, Qwen emits an incorrect 11 for the
code-output task and adds unrelated text after 391 on multiplication. Before using
a task endpoint as a utility gate, a separate prospective experiment needs a viable
dense baseline and a predeclared instruction format on fresh tasks. This release
neither changes those prompts nor reinterprets the failed exact-match criterion.

## What was frozen and retained

The protocol, source, corpus and scorer were committed and pushed as
[5998036](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/commit/59980363c2a5445242a2ab0f4e41e2bdd72fab5a) before either pretrained model saw these tasks.
The original Python 3.14.3 / torch 2.10.0+cu130 / Transformers 5.13.1 FP32 CUDA environment
was used with TF32 disabled and four CPU threads. GPU model runs were serialized.
The identical plain-text instruction is used without a chat template or added special
tokens. That format, instruction tuning, model size/training and tokenizer differences
are explicit confounds; this comparison cannot isolate an architectural effect.

Both models use their pretrained attention, normalization and residual paths with
actual one-token KV execution. Local width 8 reconstruction and full teacher-forced
layout checks precede masked conditions; layout generations must exactly equal native
dense IDs. Static selection keeps the first calibration-sorted groups; hindsight ranks
current contribution-norm scores with stable group-index ties. Nominal 90% retention
means 1008/1120 groups for Qwen and 922/1024 for OPT. OPT input biases move with groups;
output biases are charged on every visit. Selected parameter volume is not transferred
bytes or achieved memory use: the apparatus retains full weights and restoration copies.

All native/layout/masked logits, mask traces and generations are retained. Each
finite generated path is checked independently from teacher forcing. Nonfinite tensors,
invalid metric receipts and complete failure grids are preserved; invalid numerical
outputs never become valid accuracy evidence through apparently sensible token IDs.
Reconstruction metrics use their exact saved CPU tensors, avoiding GPU/CPU reduction
mismatches without relaxing the original numerical thresholds.

Independent analysis verifies committed source/configuration/protocol blobs, frozen
corpus and tokenization boundaries, pinned checkpoint/parent catalogs, all saved-logit
metrics, generated text and scoring, complete mask/observation grids, bias accounting,
and every global/domain aggregate. Restoring the release assets must reproduce analysis
exactly without pretrained rescoring. The prospective apparatus passed 171 CPU tests in
both available PyTorch environments; the integrated release suite adds the hardware
fixtures for 182 tests, with clean-tip verification retained in the publication receipt.

This closes bounded [#20](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/issues/20), while held-out quality [#8](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/issues/8)
and broader model generalization [#13](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/issues/13) remain open. The next decisive
question is still whether causally available partial execution evidence can request
economical repair. [#19](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/issues/19) covers current input, observed history,
residency and charged probes/abstention; physical paging and refinement runtime remain
gated on the **complete causal policy**. No runtime, memory saving or speedup is claimed.

[Complete task and domain results](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/blob/v0.10.0/docs/balanced-development-results.md),
[all generated continuations](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/blob/v0.10.0/docs/balanced-development-generations.md),
[prospective protocol](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/blob/v0.10.0/docs/balanced-development-protocol.md),
[archive and restoration](https://github.com/displague/dynamic-model-loading/tree/v0.10.0/results/balanced-control-20260911).

issues.title: Qualify the dense chat interface and fresh balanced task baseline
issues.body:
Qualify the pinned Qwen instruction interface independently of causal repair. Preserve v0.10 and its 0/10 plain-text result.

The prospective dense-interface protocol freezes a paired plain/chat debug comparison on the ten old tasks and a new 20-task balanced development set. Compare native library generation, incremental dense execution, and fully retained instrumented/repacked execution with identical tokens, greedy decoding and EOS. Save raw continuations and decision logits; replay native prefixes when paths diverge. Separate answer correctness, format compliance and their conjunction.

Qualification requires at least 7/10 debug and 14/20 fresh native chat successes, at least 2/4 per fresh domain, and every dense path passing frozen reference-fidelity checks. Publish failures without replacing tasks or changing criteria. These are small development fixtures, not held-out agent quality or code synthesis evidence.

Gate A governs utility claims only. Analytical repair in #19 continues independently; physical paging #11 and refinement runtime #16 remain gated on complete causal-policy quality and fully charged economics. Follow docs/adr/0002-qualified-utility-and-causal-evidence.md and docs/dense-interface-protocol.md.


Delivered in v0.11.0: native chat 7/10 debug and 12/20 fresh; matched plain 0/10. Both incremental/repacked paths match all 40 native continuations, with all numerical checks passing. Gate A fails the frozen 14/20 fresh and 2/4 per-domain criteria (topic changes 1/4). The bounded experiment is complete; the qualification hypothesis is not supported. Full raw rows and logits are preserved, with independent/restored analysis and 188-test clean-tip validation in both environments. See docs/dense-interface-results.md and docs/releases/v0.11.0.md.

issues.title: Test one-round partial evidence against matched acquisition controls
issues.body:
Deliver a bounded own-trajectory test under #19, following ADRs 0001/0002 and docs/causal-evidence-protocol.md. Preserve all earlier failures and keep physical paging gated.

Freeze two calibration passes on four separate training prefixes, four reused Wiki development prefixes, and the twenty balanced chat-development tasks from the dense-interface experiment. Train input-only, input/history and partial-evidence rankers plus a distinct detector on approximate/corrected calibration states. Dense labels never enter development decisions or state.

Compare ten policies, including larger one-shot selection, resident-first predetermined additions, partial-evidence repair at 28/56 additions, no repair, input-only ablation, detector/fallback and full completion. Every initial and corrective mask is recomputed on the policy's own trajectory. Within the 2 GiB total FFN working budget, both sparse and dense paths reserve 256 MiB for gathered device batches, canonical packing buffers and activation scratch. Sparse policies additionally share a charged 32 MiB controller reservation and resident core, so equal cardinality means equal cold bytes per layer visit. One corrective round only; no probes in this first diagnostic.

Retain calibration examples/fits, permitted-observation/state and ranking receipts, exact masks, logits, generated continuations, per-document failures, bytes, rounds and fallback counts. Measure controller/observation/update and down-product primitives. Characterize the exact resident and cold batch sizes using the v0.9 gathering/staging/transfer/packing/execution recipe; do not let coarse grid rounding determine apparent headroom.

Gate B uses completed-policy PPL <=1.01 on aggregate and each Wiki prefix. Gate C requires >=10% warm byte saving and positive fully charged serialized primitive headroom; these are plausibility conditions, not achieved latency. Partial evidence must beat both matched one-shot and predetermined controls without worse individual prefix quality before it earns an advantage claim. Dense task qualification remains a separate Gate A, and this small development sample is not held-out agent quality.

Close this bounded delivery with complete findings even if all policies fail. Keep broader #19, held-out #8, physical paging #11 and refinement runtime #16 distinct.
